This Legendary set showcases the jaw-dropping moments that have ignited arenas and left fans in awe, featuring the NHL's brightest talents at the peak of their performance.  Each Multi Highlight in this set captures the essence of excitement and skill that defines these stars. From gravity-defying goals to astonishing saves and incredible assists, Etched In Ice brings the on-ice brilliance of these players to life.

description:
Alex Ovechkin, the Washington Capitals’ electrifying superstar, has authored one of the most legendary careers in NHL history. Selected first overall in the 2004 NHL Draft, he burst onto the scene with a spectacular 52-goal, 106-point rookie season in 2005-06, capturing the Calder Trophy and launching a career defined by relentless scoring and unforgettable moments. Known for his devastating one-timer from the left faceoff circle, the ‘Great 8’ has overwhelmed goaltenders for over two decades with a combination of raw power, precision, and intensity. He holds the NHL record with nine Maurice “Rocket” Richard Trophies as the league’s top goal scorer, along with three Hart Trophies as league MVP. In 2018, he led the Capitals to their first Stanley Cup in franchise history, earning the Conn Smythe Trophy as playoff MVP.  
For years, Ovechkin has pursued the seemingly unreachable—Wayne Gretzky’s all-time goals record of 894. Entering the April 4, 2025 game against the Chicago Blackhawks just two goals shy of tying ‘The Great One,’ Ovechkin wasted no time igniting the crowd with a first-period goal to move within one. Then, with the game tied in the third period and the Capitals on the power play, the moment arrived. From his familiar spot in the left circle, Ovechkin blasted home the game-winner—goal number 894—matching Gretzky’s mark and tying the most prolific goal-scoring career the NHL has ever seen. The tally also made history in another category, as he passed Jaromir Jagr for the most game-winning goals in league history.  
This highlight captures Ovechkin standing on the doorstep of immortality—tied with Gretzky, with the next goal set to officially crown him as the NHL’s all-time goal king. A career built on passion, perseverance, and pure goal-scoring brilliance now sits at the edge of the ultimate milestone.

description:
After capturing the Calder Trophy in 2019-20, Cale Makar's meteoric rise continued as he claimed both the Conn Smythe Trophy and the Norris Trophy just two seasons later, capping off his remarkable year with his first Stanley Cup victory. This multi-highlight celebrates that unforgettable season. 
In December 2021, Makar showcased his brilliance in Philadelphia, going end-to-end and weaving through multiple Flyers defenders before roofing a stunning goal top shelf. Then, during the 2022 Stanley Cup Final against the Tampa Bay Lightning, Makar struck again with a shorthanded goal in Game 2. Starting on the penalty kill in the defensive zone, he collected the puck near the slot and led a 2-on-1 rush, finishing with a pinpoint wrist shot into the far side of the net. 
Earlier in those same playoffs, during the First Round against the Nashville Predators, Makar delivered another highlight-reel goal that displayed his speed, creativity, and elusiveness. After gaining possession near the offensive blue line, he evaded pressure with a quick deke, skated down the wall, and finished by shelving the puck past the netminder. Makar led all defensemen during the 2022 Stanley Cup Playoffs with 8 goals, 21 assists and 29 points.

description:
Hart Trophy winner, Nathan MacKinnon has been a dominant force for the Colorado Avalanche throughout his first 11 seasons. His impact on the NHL was immediate, earning the Calder Trophy during his rookie campaign in 2013-14.  
In the first highlight sequence, MacKinnon’s explosive skating is on full display as he blows past the Islanders' defense and scores a breathtaking goal during his rookie season. The second sequence showcases his relentless determination in a December 2018 game against the Coyotes. MacKinnon starts by delivering a big hit to keep the puck in the zone, causing a turnover. Later in the shift, he regains possession, fakes a shot to outmaneuver a defender, and fires a goal past the goaltender.  
In his ninth NHL season, MacKinnon captured his first Stanley Cup in 2022. During the Western Conference Second Round, he delivered the signature goal of the playoffs. In Game 5 against the St. Louis Blues, MacKinnon picked up the puck deep behind his own goal line and went coast-to-coast, scoring a sensational goal—his third of the game. Hats rained down from the home crowd, who were left in awe of his brilliance.

description:
Entering the 2024-25 season, Connor McDavid has solidified his dominance in the NHL over nine remarkable seasons. The 3-time Hart Trophy, 5-time Art Ross Trophy, Maurice Richard Trophy, and Conn Smythe Trophy winner has accumulated 982 points, leading the league by 141 points since his debut. Known for his extraordinary skill and relentless drive, McDavid has delivered countless unforgettable plays throughout his career.  
One iconic moment occurred during the "Battle of Alberta" in the 2022 Stanley Cup Playoffs when McDavid clinched the series in Game 5 with an overtime goal, marking his first playoff overtime winner. In the 2024 Stanley Cup Playoffs, where McDavid earned the Conn Smythe Trophy, he broke Wayne Gretzky’s single playoff season assist record. A highlight from that run was his signature assist in Game 5 of the Stanley Cup Final, where he set up Corey Perry for the game winning goal. Additionally, in the Western Conference Final against Dallas, McDavid scored a sensational goal in Game 6 to clinch the series, further cementing his legacy as one of the game's all-time greats.

description:
Matthew Tkachuk made an immediate impact after joining the Florida Panthers for the 2022-23 season, revitalizing the team and leading them to the Stanley Cup Final in his first year. Although they fell short in 2023, Tkachuk was the standout of those playoffs, scoring 11 goals, including four game-winners—three of which came in overtime. His relentless determination and competitive spirit reshaped the team's mindset, setting the stage for their Stanley Cup victory just one season later in 2024.  
Tkachuk's heroics were particularly evident in the 2023 Eastern Conference Final against the Carolina Hurricanes. In Game 1, which extended to four overtime periods, he netted the winner in Carolina. He followed up in Game 2 with another game-winning goal, this time in the first overtime, still on the road. Finally, in Game 4, with only five seconds remaining in the third period, Tkachuk scored the series-clinching goal, sending the home Panthers crowd into a frenzy and cementing his legacy as the hero of that series.

description:
Since Sidney Crosby joined the NHL in the 2005-06 season, no player has amassed more points than he has. A proven winner on every stage, Crosby first claimed gold at the 2005 World Junior Championship. He then earned global recognition at the 2010 Winter Olympics in Vancouver, where he famously scored the overtime game-winning goal to secure gold for Team Canada. His success continued as he captained Canada to a second consecutive Olympic gold in 2014. The following year, he led the team to victory at the World Championship in Prague, making him a member of the prestigious Triple Gold Club—the only player to have captained all three winning teams. In 2016, Crosby once again led Canada to gold at the World Cup of Hockey, where he was unanimously voted MVP.  
In the NHL, Crosby has captained the Pittsburgh Penguins to three Stanley Cup championships. One iconic moment came in 2009 during Game 4 of the Stanley Cup Final, where Crosby scored a crucial game-winning goal to tie the series against Detroit, ultimately leading the Penguins to a seven-game victory and his first Stanley Cup championship. In March 2018, Crosby showcased his incredible hand-eye coordination by juggling the puck to himself before batting it out of the air and into the net. Another standout moment occurred during the 2016 Stanley Cup Final against Tampa Bay in Game 2, where Crosby netted the overtime winner to even the series at home. That year, he claimed the Conn Smythe Trophy, an honor he would win again the following season.
